about.title: Taft Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Taft is a small city, but its traffic doesn't stay small on weekend nights. Public crash records show 22 injury collisions and 31 people hurt in the most recent year, with two lives lost, and Saturday evenings between 7 and 9 p.m. showing up again and again as the busiest window for reported crashes. Corridors like Rt 33, 6th Street, Kern Street, and Gardner Field Road carry the bulk of local traffic and, with it, the bulk of local collisions. If you were hurt in one of these, the days right after matter: photos fade, witnesses move on, and insurance adjusters start building their file immediately. Our team reviews what happened and explains your options before you say anything you can't take back to an insurance company.
commonInjuries: Torn ligaments and soft tissue damage
Cuts, bruising, and lacerations from broken glass

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash to file a car accident claim, but if a government-owned road or vehicle was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Waiting to sort out fault or injuries can quietly cost you your right to sue.

items.title: Comparative Fault Means Partial Blame Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California lets you recover damages even if you were partly at fault for the crash; your share of fault simply reduces your award rather than eliminating it. We can help make sure the insurer isn't inflating your percentage of blame to shrink what you're owed.

items.title: No Cap on Pain-and-Suffering, No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a standard car accident case, so those losses deserve real evaluation, not a quick lowball. We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover something.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's usually best to hold off. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to shrink or deny your claim, even when you're just trying to explain what happened. Speaking with us first, at no cost, can help you understand what you're required to share and what you're not.

items.question: My crash happened on Rt 33 or Gardner Field Road — does that change anything?
items.answer: Not necessarily for how fault is decided, but the road involved can matter if a public entity owned or maintained it, since claims against government agencies in California often carry a much shorter filing deadline. It's worth having us check who's responsible for that stretch of road early, rather than later.

items.question: How much will it cost me to talk to an attorney about my Taft accident?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. Our initial case review is free, and we work on contingency, so we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after you talk with us.
